newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT-Russia's Vimpel looking hot for IPO.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT-Russia's Vimpel looking hot for IPO.

text.p: Investors are driving up demand for shares of Vimpel Communications, Russia's largest cellular telecommunications company which is making its New York Stock Exchange debut tomorrow.
Vimpel is offering 5.24 million American Depositary Shares (ADS), which are due to price tonight for trading tomorrow.

The price tag to get in on the IPO was raised in response to strong demand from a range of $19.50 to $20.50 for each share, from its previous estimated range of $15.75 to $18.75, according to lead underwriter Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.

"The increase in the price range really verifies my feeling that deal will do well. Before I thought it would rise a point or more, now it's probably more like two. People really like their story," said Vincent Slavin, IPO analysts for Cantor Fitzgerald.
John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket, said he expected Vimpel to be one of the hottest new issues this week.

Vimpel markets its services under the brand name "Bee Line," primarily in the Moscow area, covering a population of about 15 million. The company said it operates the only Digital Advanced Mobile Phone System (AMPS) 800 MHz cellular system in the Moscow license area, and is the only company granted a personal communications services (PCS) license in that area.
Vimpel has also said it has licenses to operate AMPS networks in six other Russian regions -- Samara, Tver, Vladimir, Novgorod, Ryazan and the Leningrad Region excluding St. Petersburg.
Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette is the lead manager of the offering in the United States. The shares are expected to trade on the NYSE under the symbol "VIP".
